title: Energy Threat Analysis Center Act of 2026
official_title: To amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize the Department of Energy's Energy Sector Operational Support for Cyberresilience Program to provide operational support for energy sector cybersecurity and resilience.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL) and passed the House by voice vote (no recorded roll call); the bill reauthorizes an existing Department of Energy energy-sector cybersecurity program and now awaits Senate consideration.
summary: Continues a Department of Energy program that helps protect the country's energy systems — the energy sector — from cyberattacks by sharing threat information between the government and energy companies. It renews the program's funding authorization for five more years and lets the Department run it through a dedicated Energy Threat Analysis Center.
brief: Reauthorizes the Department of Energy's energy-sector cybersecurity support program through fiscal year 2031 and authorizes an Energy Threat Analysis Center to carry it out.

top_lines.headline: What the Cyberresilience Program Does
subs: Shares classified and unclassified cyber threat information with the energy sector
Jointly analyzes threats to energy systems and recommends fixes
Builds technical infrastructure for advanced analytics on energy-sector threats

top_lines.headline: What This Bill Changes
subs: Extends the program's authorization from fiscal years 2022-2026 to 2027-2031
Authorizes an Energy Threat Analysis Center at one or more physical locations
Makes program participation a discretionary, unreviewable choice of the Secretary

top_lines.headline: Information Handling Rules
subs: Information shared under the program is exempt from Freedom of Information Act disclosure
Shared information deemed voluntarily shared and withheld from the public without discretion
Program is not an advisory committee under federal advisory-committee law

items.main: Names the Act the "Energy Threat Analysis Center Act of 2026".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Energy Sector Operational Support for Cyberresilience Program

items.main: Amends Section 40125(c) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18724(c)) to add a new stated purpose of strengthening the collective defense, response, and resilience of the U.S. energy sector.
items.detail: The new purpose directs the program to enhance government-energy sector collaboration to analyze threats and deny, disrupt, and mitigate operational impacts to energy systems — by exchanging information at classified and unclassified levels and by building technical infrastructure to house, access, and perform advanced analytics. It also directs the program to advance understanding of national security risks and vulnerabilities and of threat-actor tactics, techniques, and procedures. The existing purposes are redesignated as subparagraphs (B) through (F), and one redesignated subparagraph (F) is struck.

items.main: Authorizes the Secretary to carry out program activities through an Energy Threat Analysis Center, which may be established at one or more physical locations.
items.detail: The Center is added as a new paragraph (2). The Secretary may use it to carry out any activity of the program developed under paragraph (1); the bill does not require that the Center be established or specify a location.

items.main: Sets the terms on which program assistance is provided and shields program-related information from disclosure.
items.detail: Provision of assistance or information is at the sole and unreviewable discretion of the Secretary and creates no right or benefit to similar assistance for any other entity. The program is not an advisory committee under chapter 10 of title 5. Information shared by or with federal, State, Tribal, or local governments is deemed voluntarily shared, exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552), and withheld without discretion under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3)(B) and any State, Tribal, or local disclosure law.

items.main: Extends the program's authorization of appropriations from fiscal years 2022 through 2026 to fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
items.detail: The change is made by striking "2022 through 2026" and inserting "2027 through 2031" in the redesignated authorization paragraph (renumbered from paragraph (2) to paragraph (6)). The bill states no dollar figure for the authorization.

underreported.summary: Information shared under the program with or by federal, State, Tribal, or local governments is deemed voluntarily shared, exempt from the Freedom of Information Act, and withheld from the public without discretion, overriding State, Tribal, and local disclosure laws.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill is titled and structured as a program reauthorization, but subsection (c)(5) also creates a standing public-disclosure exemption that reaches State, Tribal, and local records laws, not only federal FOIA.

underreported.summary: Program assistance and information are provided at the sole and unreviewable discretion of the Secretary and create no enforceable right or benefit for any entity to similar assistance.
underreported.why_unreported: The reauthorization label suggests continuity, but this clause forecloses judicial review of who receives program assistance and bars entities from claiming equal access.

gaps: The bill authorizes an Energy Threat Analysis Center but does not specify where it will be located, how it will be staffed, or a deadline to establish it.
The bill reauthorizes the program's appropriations for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 but states no dollar amount for that authorization.
The bill extends and expands a threat-information-sharing program but does not set any reporting requirement to Congress on the program's activities or results.

added: New program purpose to strengthen the collective defense, response, and resilience of the U.S. energy sector through government-industry threat analysis and collaboration
Authority to carry out the program through an Energy Threat Analysis Center at one or more physical locations

New provisions making program assistance discretionary and unreviewable, exempting the program from advisory-committee law, and exempting shared information from Freedom of Information Act and State/Tribal/local disclosure
modified: Reauthorizes appropriations for the Energy Sector Operational Support for Cyberresilience Program: fiscal years 2022 through 2026 → fiscal years 2027 through 2031
removed: Strikes one existing program-purpose subparagraph (redesignated subparagraph (F)) of Section 40125(c)(1)
